claims.text: A Cu-containing high-entropy alloy coating based on the Al-Cr-Cu-Fe-Ni system will adhere effectively to a Cu matrix.
Incorporated Cu promotes metallurgical compatibility between the HEA coating and the Cu matrix.
The Cu-containing coating forms a graded interface with the Cu matrix.
A graded interface minimizes thermal and compositional mismatch.
Reduced interfacial mismatch enhances the wear resistance of the coated Cu matrix.
Laser cladding or thermal spraying can be used to deposit an AlCrCuFeNi coating on a Cu matrix.
Controlled cooling and a protective atmosphere can minimize interfacial thermal stresses during coating deposition.
Cu in the HEA creates a compositional gradient at the coating-substrate interface.
The Cu-induced interfacial gradient reduces crystallographic mismatch.
The Cu-induced interfacial gradient reduces thermal-expansion mismatch.
Cu content facilitates metallurgical bonding by reducing interfacial chemical disparities.
Cu content facilitates metallurgical bonding by reducing interfacial thermal disparities.
Improved interfacial bonding produces a more robust and adherent coating.
The Cu-containing HEA coating retains the excellent wear resistance attributed to HEAs.
The Cu-containing HEA coating will markedly improve wear resistance relative to uncoated Cu.
A Cu-free HEA coating is expected to have inferior interfacial bonding compared with the Cu-containing HEA coating.
A Cu-free HEA coating is expected to have inferior wear performance compared with the Cu-containing HEA coating.
Extreme thermal gradients or improper deposition parameters may negate the proposed benefits of the compositional gradient.
